newsitem.title: USA: Saxton cautions Fed on interest rate hikes.
newsitem.headline: Saxton cautions Fed on interest rate hikes.

text.p: Joint Economic Committee of Congress Chairman Jim Saxton on Friday said he did not believe that strong economic growth in itself was inflationary or justified an interest rate increase by the Federal Reserve.
Saxton, a New Jersey Republican, said there is agreement that price stability should be implemented using inflation targets based on broad price indexes.

"In the absence of inflation shown in these indexes or forward-looking inflation measures, I do not believe that strong economic growth is itself inflationary, or justification for increases in interest rates by the Federal Reserve," he said.
Saxton issued his statement following a release by the Labor Department showing that unemployment fell to 4.9 percent in April, the lowest level in 24 years.
"This business cycle expansion continues to produce output and employment gains with no evidence of a significant slowdown in the near future," he said.
But he added that unfortunately, middle class earnings continued to show stagnation through the first quarter.
